documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside hospital - surgical oncology discharge summary
Admitted 01/03/2023, discharged 01/13/2023
Patient: Vernon Simard, DOB 01/19/1956

Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head (remnant pancreas) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy; prior distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy (2013).
Procedure 01/03/2023: completion total pancreatectomy with biliary and enteric reconstruction, through a midline incision.
Course: uneventful recovery. Diet advanced. Biliary stent removed with the specimen. Insulin requirements established with endocrine input.
Discharge medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals per the attached sliding scale; pancrelipase 36,000 lipase units with meals; tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; multivitamin daily; lactulose 15 mL twice daily as needed.
Follow-up: surgical clinic 2 weeks; oncology; endocrinology in about 6 weeks; PCP within 1 week.
Final pathology to be reviewed with oncology.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 6 days after discharge (completion total pancreatectomy 1/3).
Feels weak but walking the house a few times a day. Eating small meals, taking enzymes with each. Incision sore, no drainage. Stools soft, no grease.
Insulin: glargine 24 at bedtime and lispro by the hospital scale with meals - wife doing the math with him. Readings 90s-250s, scattered.
Not yellow. No fever.
Exam: weight 60 kg. Anicteric. Lungs clear. RRR. Midline incision healing, staples out, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near the wound, no ascites. No edema.
Med rec done against the discharge list; glargine 10 entry replaced by the new regimen.
A/P: s/p completion total pancreatectomy, now fully insulin- and enzyme-dependent. BMP today. Reviewed lows again; glucagon to be discussed with endocrinology (appt 2/13). Surgery f/u next week.

documents.title: Low sugars
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Wife calling. For about 2 weeks he has had spells a couple of hours after lunch or dinner: shaky, sweaty, heart racing, irritable, once a little confused. Meter 52 and 61 during two of them. Each time juice or crackers fixed it within minutes. No passing out, no seizures. Hungry between meals.
Advised: check before driving, carry glucose tabs, treat <70 with 15 g and recheck. Routed to PCP and faxed log to endocrinology.

documents.title: RE: Low sugars
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Spoke with endocrinology nurse; they will keep the 2/13 visit and call him this week about the lispro scale. Wife knows to call 911 if he can't swallow juice.

conditions.label: Post-pancreatectomy hypoglycemia due to glucagon deficiency

medications.sig: Spray 3 mg into one nostril once for severe low blood sugar; may repeat in 15 minutes

documents.title: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology - consultation
Seen 02/13/2023
Patient: Vernon Simard, 67 M

Reason: low blood sugars after total pancreatectomy.
Six weeks ago he had a completion total pancreatectomy for a pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, after a 2013 distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy. Diabetes was diagnosed last August and he has used insulin injections since.
For the past month he has had episodes several times a week, a few hours after meals, of shakiness, anxiety and palpitations that settle quickly with juice or a snack. His wife sees him sweaty, irritable and briefly confused during them. He is hungrier between meals and has lost another 5 lb. Good adherence; keeps all appointments. No fever, chest pain or recent illness.
History: alcohol-related cirrhosis and chronic pancreatitis, CAD with stent, BPH. Former smoker (about 40 pack-years), quit in May 2022. No alcohol since early 2021. Retired truck driver.
Family: mother with type 2 diabetes.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; insulin lispro sliding scale with meals; tamsulosin 0.4 mg; aspirin 81 mg; atorvastatin 40 mg; pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals; multivitamin; lactulose 15 mL BID prn. NKDA.
Exam: well-healing midline scar. Neuro nonfocal. Heart, lungs and abdomen normal.

Assessment: post-pancreatectomy hypoglycemia with loss of glucagon counter-regulation, in insulin-requiring diabetes after total pancreatectomy.
Plan:
- Lower the lispro correction scale (new scale given); skip lispro if he eats less than half a meal.
- Smaller, more frequent meals with protein; bedtime snack.
- Glucose tablets on him at all times; glucagon nasal powder 3 mg prescribed for severe lows, wife taught.
- Continue glargine 24 units for now.
- Return in 3 months with meter download.
Endocrinology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
10 weeks post completion pancreatectomy. Endocrinology letter reviewed: glucagon-deficiency lows, lispro scale lowered, glucagon nasal spray at home.
Lows now about once a week and mild, all after a big lunch with full lispro - he's learning. Snacks between meals. Weight 58.5, up a little from the endo visit. Surgery cleared him. Oncology plan is surveillance scans.
Exam: anicteric. Lungs clear. RRR. Incision well healed. Abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema. No bruising.
Labs today: CBC, CMP, INR, A1c.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Platelets 230, INR 1.2, bili and alk phos back near normal. The coagulation problem oncology called chronic DIC has resolved with the tumor out - removing from active list. A1c 7.3. Sent to pt.

documents.title: PA - glucagon nasal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy needed PA for glucagon 3 mg nasal powder (prescribed by endocrinology). Submitted with dx insulin-treated diabetes with recurrent hypoglycemia after total pancreatectomy. Approved. Endo office aware.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Wife present.
Year in review: pancreatic head cancer treated with chemo and completion total pancreatectomy (1/3/23), now on oncology surveillance. Diabetes on glargine 24 + lispro scale; lows after pancreatectomy managed by endocrinology. Sober since Feb 2021, off cigarettes since May 2022. PHQ-2 1, AUDIT-C 0.
Functional: independent ADLs, wife handles meds and pharmacy. No falls. Not driving long distances.
Advance care planning (25 min): reviewed goals. He wants full treatment including ICU if there is a good chance of getting back home; does not want to be kept on machines long term if he won't recover. Wife remains HCP. MOLST not completed today; will consider.
Exam: weight 59.5. Anicteric. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft, midline scar healed, no ascites. Feet: intact sensation to monofilament, pulses palpable, skin intact.
Plan: lipids, urine microalbumin, A1c, BMP. Diabetic eye exam referral. Vaccines in the fall.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Weight 61 kg, up from 58 in the spring - eating 5 small meals, enzymes with each. Lows down to 1-2 a month, mild, no glucagon needed. Endocrinology adjusted nothing further at the June visit per pt. Oncology scan in August clear per pt.
Exam: anicteric. Lungs clear. RRR. Abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema.
A/P: weight loss has turned around - off the problem list. Diabetes: A1c today; continue glargine 24 + lispro scale. Cirrhosis: CMP/CBC. Flu and updated COVID today.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home with wife, identity confirmed.
Winter check-in. Feels steady. Oncology surveillance CT last week reviewed with him there - no sign of recurrence, next in 6 months. Sugars mostly 110-220; one low last month, treated with tabs. Still sober, still not smoking.
No jaundice, no swelling, no confusion per wife.
Plan: refills sent (glargine, lispro, pen needles, pancrelipase). In-person visit in March with labs.

documents.title: Bruises
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Denise writing. Vernon has been more tired the last few weeks and is getting bruises on his arms and legs from nothing. His belly looks bigger too. He has his GI liver appointment on the 20th already. Should he wait for that or come in?

documents.title: RE: Bruises
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. If there is no bleeding (black stools, vomiting blood, nosebleeds that won't stop), no fever and no confusion, it's reasonable to keep the GI visit on the 20th. If any of those happen, go to the ED. I'll see him after GI - the front desk will call to book.

reports.text: Liver small and nodular with coarse echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion. Portal vein patent. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilation. Postsurgical absence of the pancreas and spleen. Ascites present in the abdomen. Kidneys normal without hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic liver without focal lesion. Ascites. No biliary dilation.

documents.title: Gastroenterology letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology / hepatology - clinic note
Visit 02/20/2024
Re: Vernon Simard, 68 M

Seen for fatigue and increased bruising over several weeks. He takes a multivitamin and aspirin 81 mg; no anticoagulant.
Background: alcohol-related cirrhosis (abstinent since early 2021), chronic pancreatitis, two pancreatic adenocarcinomas (2013 distal pancreatectomy/splenectomy; 2023 completion total pancreatectomy, on oncology surveillance), CAD with stent, insulin-treated diabetes, Zenker diverticulum treated 2022.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro sliding scale, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals, lactulose 15 mL BID prn. NKDA.

Exam: scleral icterus. Abdomen distended with shifting dullness. Spider angiomata on the chest. Multiple ecchymoses on the arms and legs. Spleen surgically absent. No JVD. Neurologic exam normal; mental status intact.

Labs and ultrasound ordered today. Results: bilirubin about 3, albumin under 3, INR 1.7, platelets in the 130s, mild hyponatremia. Ultrasound: cirrhotic liver, no mass, ascites, no biliary dilation.

Impression: decompensated alcohol-related cirrhosis with new ascites and coagulopathy of liver disease explaining the bruising. No sign of biliary obstruction or a liver mass.
Plan: 2 g sodium diet; continued abstinence; labs with PCP in 2 weeks; return here in 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Follow-up after GI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
GI letter reviewed: decompensated cirrhosis - ascites, jaundice, coagulopathy; US without mass or duct dilation.
He feels tired but no worse. Bruises still coming up easily. Belly full, pants tighter; weight 63 (61 in September). Following the low-salt diet - wife reading labels. Still no alcohol. No confusion, no black stools, no vomiting blood.
Exam: mild scleral icterus. Spider angiomata on the upper chest. Several ecchymoses on forearms and shins. Abdomen distended with shifting dullness, nontender. No asterixis. No edema.
A/P:
1. Decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis with ascites and coagulopathy. CMP, CBC, INR today for GI. Reinforced 2 g sodium. Bleeding precautions. GI follow-up May.
2. Diabetes: A1c today. Lows rare.
3. CAD: continue aspirin and atorvastatin.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bili 3.1, albumin 2.8, INR 1.7, plt 132, Na 133, Cr normal. A1c 7.2. Copied to GI.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 days of burning with urination and going more often. Some low back ache. No fever, no chills, no blood in urine, no flank pain. Tamsulosin unchanged.
Exam: afebrile. Abdomen soft, mild distension with shifting dullness unchanged. No CVA tenderness.

A/P: UTI in a man with BPH. TMP-SMX DS BID x 7 days. Fluids. Call if fever or worse.

documents.title: Feeling better
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The antibiotic worked, no burning anymore. Thanks. -Vernon (Denise typing)

documents.title: RE: Feeling better

documents.body: Glad to hear it. See you at the wellness visit in June.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. With wife.
Continuing GI follow-up; still on the low-salt diet. Oncology surveillance stable per pt. Endocrinology yearly now. Sober 3+ years, smoke-free 2 years.
Independent in ADLs; wife does IADLs (meds, finances, driving more). No falls. PHQ-2 1. Hearing and vision OK.
ACP reviewed, unchanged; wife HCP.
Exam: weight as charted. Mild icterus. Abdomen with shifting dullness, unchanged. Feet: sensation intact, no ulcers.
Plan: lipids, urine microalbumin. Eye exam due. Fall vaccines: flu, COVID, RSV, and MenACWY booster (5 years since 2019).

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Urinary burning, frequency and low back ache came back about 3 weeks after the cipro course, since mid-November, milder but persistent. No fever, no chills.
Liver: weight 62, belly smaller; following the salt limit closely. Still sober.
Exam: afebrile. Faint scleral icterus. Abdomen soft, flat, no shifting dullness today. No edema.
A/P:
1. Recurrent/persistent lower urinary symptoms after three antibiotic courses this year - urology referral (next available February).
2. Cirrhosis: ascites no longer evident on exam. Labs today.
3. Diabetes: A1c.
